Markus / Sofia —

We reviewed the CAD and the stage sightlines. Quick take: hardware codec + redundant cloud bridge is the cleanest option for a mixed remote cohort (SIP from London, WebRTC from SF, and PSTN dial-in for a handful). Proposed stack:
- Primary: Polycom G7500 in the AV rack (HDX compatible SIP)
- Redundancy: cloud SIP bridge (AudioWorks managed) + backup local laptop running Jitsi for last-resort screen-share capture
- Mics: 3 handheld Shure ULX-D (wired diversity), 2 boundary mics for audience pickup; a separate ambient room mic for recording reference
- Recording: ISO multitrack to a local recorder (24-bit WAV) + cloud upload to our S3 bucket for sharing. Retention: Redwood asked for 90-day retention by default — we’ll set auto-delete after 120 days unless otherwise directed.

We will need: dedicated static outbound IP for the recorder to push to cloud; also prefer the whitelist for SIP ports (5060) and RTP dynamic ports 10000-20000. If Evergreen wants restricted NAT, we can proxy.

Estimate: hardware codec + install + one-day engineer onsite = $6,200 (detailed line items in attached).

Attachment: audioworks-estimate-v1.pdf

— Ben
